# Real zero polynomials need not have a real zero amalgam

It is not the case that for all block sizes $\ell, m, n$ and every degree bound $d$, if $p \in \mathbb{R}[x, y]$ and $q \in \mathbb{R}[x, z]$ ($x$, $y$, $z$ blocks of $\ell$, $m$, $n$ variables) are real zero polynomials of total degree at most $d$ with $p(x, 0) = q(x, 0)$, then some real zero polynomial $r \in \mathbb{R}[x, y, z]$ of total degree at most $d$ satisfies $r(x, y, 0) = p$ and $r(x, 0, z) = q$ (a real polynomial $p$ in variables $\sigma$ is real zero when for every real point $a$ and every complex $t$, $p(ta) = 0$ forces $t \in \mathbb{R}$; in particular $p(0) \ne 0$). Sawall and Schweighofer give cubic real zero polynomials $p \in \mathbb{R}[x, y]$ and $q \in \mathbb{R}[x, z]$ with $\ell = 6$ and $m = n = 1$, agreeing on $y = z = 0$, that have no real zero amalgam of any degree.

## Sources

- M. Schweighofer, *Spectrahedral relaxations of hyperbolicity cones*, in Real Algebraic Geometry with a View Toward Hyperbolic Programming and Free Probability, Oberwolfach Reports 17 (2020), issue 1 (Report 12/2020), 652–654, real zero amalgamation conjecture, p. 653.
- D. Sawall and M. Schweighofer, *Amalgamation of real zero polynomials*, Indag. Math. (N.S.) 35 (2024), 37–59, arXiv:2305.07403, Example 6.1.
